checks.locator: H.E.S.S. Telescopes page, 'Arrangement of the telescopes'; Crab paper (A&A 457, 899) section 2
checks.quote: The initial four H.E.S.S. telescopes (Phase I) are arranged in form of a square with 120 m side length

geometry.note: OpenStreetMap trace (rank 11), so confidence is capped at approximate even though the neighbour-distance check passes: that check confirms the telescopes' relative placement, not the outline of this polygon.

method: OpenStreetMap way 171900955 (building=yes, man_made=telescope, name=H.E.S.S., telescope:diameter=12m), a closed 7-node polygon used verbatim, no simplification. The way is one of four traced by OSM mappers at the corners of the CT1-CT4 square; OSM does not say which of CT1-CT4 it is, so the corner is named instead. The distance check measures its centroid to the centroid of the west corner telescope against the published 120 m side.
name: H.E.S.S. 12 m telescope, south corner of the CT1-CT4 square
notes: Which of CT1-CT4 stands at this corner is not stated by any fetched source (the H.E.S.S. Telescopes page says only that the square's diagonal runs north-south). Backlog: a H.E.S.S. instrument paper or array-layout table that numbers the telescopes.

summary.plain: One of the four 12-metre H.E.S.S. telescopes of the original array, at the south corner of the 120-metre square (which of CT1 to CT4 it is, is not stated in the map data).
